Text and Annotations

Source: vignettes/articles/r-docs/text-and-annotations.Rmd
text-and-annotations.Rmd

Text Mode 

library(plotly.core)

Primates <- c("Potar monkey", "Gorilla", "Human", "Rhesus monkey", "Chimp")
Bodywt <- c(10.0, 207.0, 62.0, 6.8, 52.2)
Brainwt <- c(115, 406, 1320, 179, 440)
data <- data.frame(Primates, Bodywt, Brainwt)

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Bodywt,
    y = ~Brainwt,
    mode = "text",
    text = ~Primates,
    textposition = "middle right",
    textfont = go_font(color = "#000000", size = 16)
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    title = "Primates Brain and Body Weight",
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "Body Weight (kg)", zeroline = TRUE, range = c(0, 250)),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "Brain Weight (g)", range = c(0, 1400))
  )

See more options on the textposition argument in go_scatter().

Styling Text 

library(plotly.core)

data <- mtcars[which(mtcars$am == 1 & mtcars$gear == 4), ]

t <- go_font(family = "sans serif", size = 14, color = "rgb(127, 127, 127)")

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~mpg,
    text = rownames(data),
    mode = "text",
    textfont = t,
    textposition = "top right"
  ) |>
  update_layout(xaxis = go_xaxis(range = c(1.6, 3.2)), showlegend = FALSE)

Controlling text fontsize with uniformtext

For the pie, bar, sunburst and treemap traces, it is possible to force all the text labels to have the same size thanks to the uniformtext layout parameter. The minsize attribute sets the font size, and the mode attribute sets what happens for labels which cannot fit with the desired fontsize: either hide them or show them with overflow.

library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df <- df[which(df$year == 2007 & df$continent == "Europe" & df$pop > 2.e6), ]

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_bar(
    x = ~country,
    y = ~pop,
    text = ~lifeExp,
    name = "",
    hovertemplate = paste("%{x}", "<br>lifeExp: %{text:.2s}<br>"),
    texttemplate = "%{y:.2s}",
    textposition = "outside"
  ) |>
  update_layout(uniformtext = go_uniformtext(minsize = 8, mode = "hide"))
library(plotly.core)

df <- read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plotly/datasets/master/gapminderDataFiveYear.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
df <- df[which(df$year == 2007 & df$continent == "Asia"), ]

df |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_pie(labels = ~country, values = ~pop, textposition = "inside") |>
  update_layout(uniformtext = go_uniformtext(minsize = 12, mode = "hide"))

Adding Informations to Default Hover Text 

library(plotly.core)

iris |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Petal.Length,
    y = ~Petal.Width,
    mode = "markers",
    text = ~paste("Species: ", Species)
  )

Custom Hover Text 

library(plotly.core)

iris |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~Petal.Length,
    y = ~Petal.Width,
    mode = "markers",
    hoverinfo = "text",
    text = ~paste(
      "</br> Species: ", Species,
      "</br> Petal Length: ", Petal.Length,
      "</br> Petal Width: ", Petal.Width
    )
  )

Single Annotation 

library(plotly.core)

m <- mtcars[which.max(mtcars$mpg), ]

mtcars |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = ~wt, y = ~mpg, mode = "markers") |>
  add_annotation(
    x = m$wt,
    y = m$mpg,
    text = rownames(m),
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 7,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  )

Multiple Annotations 

library(plotly.core)

data <- mtcars[which(mtcars$am == 1 & mtcars$gear == 4), ]

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~mpg,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(size = 10)
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = data$wt,
    y = data$mpg,
    text = rownames(data),
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 4,
    arrowsize = .5,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  )

Subplot Annotations 

library(plotly.core)

economics <- ggplot2::economics
m <- economics[which.max(economics$unemploy), ]
n <- economics[which.max(economics$uempmed), ]

# figure labels
f <- go_font(family = "Courier New, monospace", size = 18, color = "#7f7f7f")

make_subplots(rows = 1, cols = 2) |>
  add_scatter(
    data = economics,
    x = ~date,
    y = ~unemploy,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "unemploy",
    row = 1,
    col = 1
  ) |>
  add_scatter(
    data = economics,
    x = ~date,
    y = ~uempmed,
    mode = "lines",
    name = "uempmed",
    row = 1,
    col = 2
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = m$date,
    y = m$unemploy,
    text = "annotation a",
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 7,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = n$date,
    y = n$uempmed,
    text = "annotation b",
    xref = "x2",
    yref = "y2",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 7,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  ) |>
  update_xaxes(title = go_xaxis_title(text = "x Axis", font = f)) |>
  update_yaxes(title = go_yaxis_title(text = "y Axis", font = f))

3D Annotations 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter3d(
    x = c("2017-01-01", "2017-02-10", "2017-03-20"),
    y = c("A", "B", "C"),
    z = c(1, 1000, 100000),
    name = "z"
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    scene = go_scene(
      aspectratio = go_scene_aspectratio(x = 1, y = 1, z = 1),
      camera = go_scene_camera(
        center = go_scene_camera_center(x = 0, y = 0, z = 0),
        eye = go_scene_camera_eye(
          x = 1.96903462608,
          y = -1.09022831971,
          z = 0.405345349304
        ),
        up = go_scene_camera_up(x = 0, y = 0, z = 1)
      ),
      dragmode = "turntable",
      xaxis = go_scene_axis(title = "", type = "date"),
      yaxis = go_scene_axis(title = "", type = "category"),
      zaxis = go_scene_axis(title = "", type = "log"),
      annotations = list(
        go_scene_annotation(
          showarrow = FALSE,
          x = "2017-01-01",
          y = "A",
          z = 0,
          text = "Point 1",
          xanchor = "left",
          xshift = 10,
          opacity = 0.7
        ),
        go_scene_annotation(
          x = "2017-02-10",
          y = "B",
          z = 4,
          text = "Point 2",
          textangle = 0,
          ax = 0,
          ay = -75,
          font = go_font(color = "black", size = 12),
          arrowcolor = "black",
          arrowsize = 3,
          arrowwidth = 1,
          arrowhead = 1
        ),
        go_scene_annotation(
          x = "2017-03-20",
          y = "C",
          z = 5,
          ax = 50,
          ay = 0,
          text = "Point 3",
          arrowhead = 1,
          xanchor = "left",
          yanchor = "bottom"
        )
      )
    ),
    xaxis = go_xaxis(title = "x"),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(title = "y")
  )

Styling Annotations 

library(plotly.core)

data <- mtcars[which(mtcars$am == 1 & mtcars$gear == 4), ]

data |>
  go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(
    x = ~wt,
    y = ~mpg,
    mode = "markers",
    marker = go_scatter_marker(size = 10)
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = data$wt,
    y = data$mpg,
    text = rownames(data),
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    arrowhead = 4,
    arrowsize = .5,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40,
    # Styling annotations' text:
    font = go_font(color = "#264E86", family = "sans serif", size = 14)
  )

Set Annotation Text Anchors 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = 1, y = 1, mode = "markers", showlegend = FALSE) |>
  add_scatter(x = 1, y = 2, mode = "markers", showlegend = FALSE) |>
  add_scatter(x = 1, y = 3, mode = "markers", showlegend = FALSE) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 1,
    y = 1,
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    text = "Right Anchor",
    xanchor = "right",
    showarrow = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 1,
    y = 2,
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    text = "Center Anchor",
    xanchor = "center",
    showarrow = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 1,
    y = 3,
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    text = "Left Anchor",
    xanchor = "left",
    showarrow = FALSE
  )

Customize Displayed Text with a Text Template

To show an arbitrary text in your chart you can use texttemplate (see e.g. go_pie()), which is a template string used for rendering the information, and will override textinfo. This template string can include variables in %{variable} format, numbers in d3-format’s syntax, and date in d3-time-fomrat’s syntax. texttemplate customizes the text that appears on your plot vs. hovertemplate that customizes the tooltip text.

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_pie(
    values = c(40000000, 20000000, 30000000, 10000000),
    labels = c("Wages", "Operating expenses", "Cost of sales", "Insurance"),
    texttemplate = "%{label}: %{value:$,s} <br>(%{percent})",
    textposition = "inside"
  )

Customize Text Template

The following example uses textfont (see go_scatterternary()) to customize the added text.

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatterternary(
    a = c(3, 2, 5),
    b = c(2, 5, 2),
    c = c(5, 2, 2),
    mode = "markers+text",
    text = c("A", "B", "C"),
    texttemplate = "%{text}<br>(%{a:.2f}, %{b:.2f}, %{c:.2f})",
    textposition = "bottom center",
    textfont = go_font(
      family = "Times",
      size = c(18, 21, 20),
      color = c("IndianRed", "MediumPurple", "DarkOrange")
    )
  )

Set Date in Text Template

The following example shows how to show date by setting the axis type (see go_yaxis()) in funnel charts. As you can see textinfo and texttemplate (see go_funnel()) have the same functionality when you want to determine ‘just’ the trace information on the graph.

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_funnel(
    name = "Montreal",
    orientation = "h",
    y = c("2018-01-01", "2018-07-01", "2019-01-01", "2020-01-01"),
    x = c(100, 60, 40, 20),
    textposition = "inside",
    texttemplate = "%{y| %a. %_d %b %Y}"
  ) |>
  add_funnel(
    name = "Vancouver",
    orientation = "h",
    y = c("2018-01-01", "2018-07-01", "2019-01-01", "2020-01-01"),
    x = c(90, 70, 50, 10),
    textposition = "inside",
    textinfo = "label"
  ) |>
  update_layout(yaxis = go_yaxis(type = "date"))

Set Annotation Coordinate References 

library(plotly.core)

go_figure() |>
  add_scatter(x = 0.5, y = 1, mode = "markers", showlegend = FALSE) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 0.5,
    y = 1,
    xref = "paper",
    yref = "paper",
    text = "<b>paper reference = [0.5, 1]</b>",
    showarrow = FALSE
  ) |>
  add_annotation(
    x = 0.5,
    y = 1,
    xref = "x",
    yref = "y",
    text = "x + y reference = [0.5, 1]",
    showarrow = TRUE,
    ax = 20,
    ay = -40
  ) |>
  update_layout(
    xaxis = go_xaxis(zeroline = FALSE),
    yaxis = go_yaxis(zeroline = FALSE)
  )

See go_annotation() for more information and chart attribute options!
